title.zh: 卷二十五 列傳第十九 周捨 徐勉
title.raw: 卷二十五 列傳第十九 周捨 徐勉 Volume 25: Zhou She; Xu Mian

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第二十五 列傳第十九

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 25, Biographies 19
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 25, Biographies, Number 19

sentences.zh: 周捨 徐勉

translations.literal: Zhou She; Xu Mian
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She and Xu Mian

sentences.zh: 周捨字昇逸，汝南安城人，晉左光祿大夫顗之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhou She, styled Shengyi, was a native of Ancheng in Runan, the eighth-generation descendant of Yan, Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She, whose courtesy name was Shengyi, came from Ancheng in Runan and was the eighth-generation descendant of Yan, who had served Jin as Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父顒，齊中書侍郎，有名於時。

translations.literal: His father Yan was a Secretariat Attendant of Qi and had a reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been a Secretariat Attendant under Qi and was well known in his day.

sentences.zh: 捨幼聰潁，顒異之，臨卒謂曰：「汝不患不富貴，但當持之以道德。

translations.literal: She in youth was clever and quick; Yan regarded him as exceptional. On his deathbed he told him, "You need not worry about lacking wealth and rank, but you must uphold yourself with moral virtue."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, She was quick and clever, and Yan saw something extraordinary in him. On his deathbed Yan told him, "You need not fear that you will lack wealth and rank, but you must hold yourself to moral principle."

sentences.zh: 」旣長，博學多通，尤精義理，善誦書，背文諷說，音韻清辯。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was broadly learned and masterful in many fields, especially expert in principles of righteousness and reason. He was skilled at reciting books, could chant texts from memory, and his tones were clear and his eloquence refined.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had grown up, he was widely learned and accomplished in many subjects, especially the principles of moral reasoning. He excelled at recitation, could declaim texts from memory, and spoke with a clear voice and polished eloquence.

sentences.zh: 起家齊太學博士，遷後軍行參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as an Erudite of the Imperial Academy of Qi and was transferred to Aide to the Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as an Erudite of the Qi Imperial Academy and was later appointed Aide to the Rear General.

sentences.zh: 建武中，魏人吳包南歸，有儒學，尚書僕射江祏招包講。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era, the Wei man Wu Bao came south and returned; he had Confucian learning, and the Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Jiang Shi invited Bao to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu reign, Wu Bao, a scholar from Wei who had come south, was invited by Vice Director Jiang Shi to give lectures on the classics.

sentences.zh: 捨造坐，累折包，辭理遒逸，由是名爲口辯。

translations.literal: She took a seat and repeatedly refuted Bao; his reasoning was forceful and elegant, and from this he gained the name of a debater.
translations.idiomatic: She took a seat in the audience and repeatedly bested Bao in debate. His arguments were forceful and elegant, and from that time he was famed for his eloquence.

sentences.zh: 王亮爲丹陽尹，聞而悅之，辟爲主簿，政事多委焉。

translations.literal: Wang Liang was Intendant of Danyang; hearing of him he was pleased and recruited him as Chief Clerk, entrusting much of the administration to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Liang became Intendant of Danyang, he was delighted to hear of She and recruited him as chief clerk, delegating much of the administration to him.

sentences.zh: 遷太常丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，爲奉常丞。

translations.literal: When the Liang administration was established, he became Vice Director of Court Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was first set up, he was appointed Vice Director of Court Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 高祖卽位，博求異能之士。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, he broadly sought men of unusual ability.
translations.idiomatic: After the High Ancestor acceded, he cast a wide net for men of exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書范雲與顒素善，重捨才器，言之於高祖，召拜尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Fan Yun had long been on good terms with Yan and valued She's talent and capacity; he spoke of him to the High Ancestor, who summoned and appointed him Gentleman of the Department of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun, Minister of Personnel, had long been close to Yan and admired She's ability. He recommended him to the High Ancestor, who summoned She and appointed him Gentleman of the Sacrifices Section in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時天下草創，禮儀損益，多自捨出。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was newly founded; additions and reductions to ritual and ceremony largely came from She.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was still being founded, and most revisions to ritual and ceremonial practice came from She.

sentences.zh: 尋爲後軍記室參軍、秣陵令。

translations.literal: Soon he became Recorder of the Rear General's Staff and Magistrate of Moling.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Recorder on the staff of the Rear General and Magistrate of Moling.

sentences.zh: 入爲中書通事舍人，累遷太子洗馬，散騎常侍，中書侍郎，鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He entered the court as Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs in the Secretariat, and was repeatedly promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent, Regular Attendant, Secretariat Attendant, and Director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He entered central government as an Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs in the Secretariat and rose through the ranks to Groom of the Heir Apparent, Regular Attendant, Secretariat Attendant, and Director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 時王亮得罪歸家，故人莫有至者，捨獨敦恩舊，及卒，身營殯葬，時人稱之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Liang had offended and returned home; none of his old friends came to see him, but She alone treated him with the kindness due an old associate, and when he died personally arranged the funeral; people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Liang fell from favor and retired home, none of his old friends would visit him, but She alone remained loyal to their past friendship. When Wang died, She personally arranged the funeral, and people praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書吏部郎，太子右衛率，右衛將軍，雖居職屢徙，而常留省內，罕得休下。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and General of the Right Guard; although his posts changed repeatedly, he constantly remained within the Secretariat and rarely had leave to go home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and General of the Right Guard. Though his titles changed often, he remained at court and seldom had a day off.

sentences.zh: 國史詔誥，儀體法律，軍旅謀謨，皆兼掌之。

translations.literal: National history, imperial edicts and proclamations, ritual forms and laws, and military strategy and counsel—he held charge of them all.
translations.idiomatic: He held simultaneous responsibility for the national history, imperial edicts and proclamations, ritual protocol and law, and military planning.

sentences.zh: 日夜侍上，預機密，二十餘年未嘗離左右。

translations.literal: Day and night he attended the sovereign and took part in confidential affairs; for more than twenty years he never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he attended the emperor and shared in state secrets; for more than twenty years he was never far from his side.

sentences.zh: 捨素辯給，與人泛論談謔，終日不絕口，而竟無一言漏泄機事，衆尤嘆服之。

translations.literal: She was by nature quick in debate; with others he would discourse broadly and jest, talking without cease all day, yet in the end not a single word of confidential affairs leaked out, and the multitude especially admired and submitted to this.
translations.idiomatic: She was naturally quick-witted and loved to debate and banter with others, talking without pause all day long, yet he never let a single secret slip. People admired him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 性儉素，衣服器用，居處床席，如布衣之貧者。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal and plain; his clothes, implements, dwelling, bed, and mat were like those of a poor commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly by nature: his clothes, furnishings, room, bed, and bedding were no better than a poor commoner's.

sentences.zh: 每入官府，雖廣廈華堂，閨閤重邃，捨居之則塵埃滿積。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered an official residence, though it had broad halls and splendid chambers with inner apartments deep and secluded, where She dwelt dust would pile up thick.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he lodged in government offices, however grand the halls and chambers, his rooms were left thick with dust.

sentences.zh: 以荻爲鄣，壞亦不營。

translations.literal: He used reeds for screens; when they broke he did not repair them.
translations.idiomatic: He used reed mats for partitions and did not bother to replace them when they wore out.

sentences.zh: 爲右衛，母憂去職，起爲明威將軍、右驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: While serving as Right Guard, he left office on his mother's death; on mourning's end he was reappointed General of Illustrious Might and General of the Right Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: While he was General of the Right Guard, he left office to observe mourning for his mother. When the mourning period ended, he was reappointed General of Illustrious Might and General of the Right Swift Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除侍中，領步兵校尉，未拜，仍遷員外散騎常侍、太子左衛率。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently Colonel of the Footsoldiers; before he could take up the appointment he was transferred to Extraordinary Regular Attendant and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was named Palace Attendant and concurrent Colonel of the Footsoldiers, but before he could assume those posts he was transferred to Extraordinary Regular Attendant and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 頃之，加散騎常侍、本州大中正，遷太子詹事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was given the additional title of Regular Attendant and Chief Rectifier of his native province, and was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was given the additional titles of Regular Attendant and Chief Rectifier of his home province, and was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 普通五年，南津獲武陵太守白渦書，許遺捨面錢百萬，津司以聞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Putong, at South Ford a letter from Bai Wo, Administrator of Wuling, was seized, promising to give She a million in cash face to face; the ford office reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Putong, officials at South Ford seized a letter from Bai Wo, Administrator of Wuling, promising to pay She a million cash in person, and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 雖書自外入，猶爲有司所奏，捨坐免。

translations.literal: Although the letter came from outside, he was still impeached by the responsible officials, and She was punished by dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Even though the letter had come from outside, the authorities still impeached him, and She was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 遷右驍騎將軍，知太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Swift Cavalry and acted as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed General of the Right Swift Cavalry and served concurrently as acting Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以其年卒，時年五十六。

translations.literal: In that same year he died, at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died later that year, at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 上臨哭，哀慟左右。

translations.literal: The sovereign came in person to mourn; his grief moved those on his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn him, and his grief moved everyone around him.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太子詹事、豫州大中正捨，奄至殞喪，惻愴于懷。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Chief Rectifier of Yuzhou She has suddenly met with death; my heart is pierced with sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Chief Rectifier of Yuzhou, She, has died suddenly, and my heart is full of grief."

sentences.zh: 其學思堅明，志行開敏，劬勞機要，多歷歲年，才用未窮，彌可嗟慟。

translations.literal: His learning and thought were firm and clear, his will and conduct open and keen; he toiled at crucial affairs through many years, his talent and use not yet exhausted—how much the more lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was solid and his mind clear, his character open and his conduct sharp. He labored at the heart of government for many years, and his talents were far from spent—how deeply this grieves me.

sentences.zh: 宜隆追遠，以旌善人。

translations.literal: It is fitting to elevate remembrance of the distant and thereby honor a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Let us honor the dead and thereby commend a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、護軍將軍，鼓吹一部，給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，喪事隨由資給。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, one set of ceremonial music, the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and funeral expenses supplied as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, with one band of ceremonial music, the secret funerary vessels from the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, and whatever funds the funeral requires.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jianzi, "the Plain."

sentences.zh: 」明年，又詔曰：「故侍中、護軍將軍簡子捨，義該玄儒，博窮文史，奉親能孝，事君盡忠，歷掌機密，清貞自居。

translations.literal: The next year, another edict said: "The late Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, Jianzi She, embraced the meaning of the profound Ruists and exhaustively mastered literature and history; in serving his parents he could be filial, in serving his lord he was wholly loyal; through successive terms he held confidential affairs and kept himself pure and upright."
translations.idiomatic: The following year another edict read: "The late Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army, Jianzi She, embodied the deepest Confucian learning and mastered literature and history. He was filial to his parents and wholly loyal to his sovereign. He held confidential posts for years and lived in unstained integrity."

sentences.zh: 食不重味，身靡兼衣。

translations.literal: In food he did not repeat flavors; on his person he did not wear layered garments.
translations.idiomatic: He never ate two dishes of the same kind at one meal, and never wore more than one layer of clothing at a time.

sentences.zh: 終亡之日，內無妻妾，外無田宅，兩兒單貧，有過古烈。

translations.literal: On the day of his final death he had no wife or concubine within, no fields or residence without; his two sons were alone and poor—he surpassed the stern worthies of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he had no wife or concubine at home and no fields or house abroad. His two sons were left alone in poverty—a austerity that surpassed the stern worthies of old.

sentences.zh: 往者，南司白渦之劾，恐外議謂朕有私，致此黜免，追愧若人一介之善。

translations.literal: Formerly, in the impeachment by the southern office concerning Bai Wo, I feared outside opinion would say I had private motives and so caused this dismissal; looking back, I regret losing even one man's small measure of goodness.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern office impeached him over Bai Wo, I feared people would think I acted from private motives and allowed his dismissal. Looking back, I regret having lost even one man's small measure of goodness.

sentences.zh: 外可量加褒異，以旌善人。

translations.literal: Externally he may be given additional honors according to measure, to commend a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Let additional honors be granted as befits the case, to commend a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 」二子：弘義，弘信。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Hongyi and Hongxin.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Hongyi and Hongxin.

sentences.zh: 徐勉字脩仁，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Mian, styled Xiuren, was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian, whose courtesy name was Xiuren, came from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 祖長宗，宋高祖霸府行參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Changzong was Aide on the March of the Song High Ancestor's hegemonial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Changzong had served the Song founder as Aide on the staff of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 父融，南昌相。

translations.literal: His father Rong was Chancellor of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong had been Chancellor of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 勉幼孤貧，早勵清節。

translations.literal: Mian in youth was orphaned and poor and early cultivated pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Mian lost his father young and grew up poor, but from an early age he cultivated a life of integrity.

sentences.zh: 年六歲，時屬霖雨，家人祈霽，率爾爲文，見稱耆宿。

translations.literal: At age six, when there was prolonged rain, the family prayed for clear skies; he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six, during a long spell of rain, his family prayed for clear weather. He spontaneously composed a piece of writing and was praised by the elders.

sentences.zh: 及長，篤志好學。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was steadfast in will and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to study.

sentences.zh: 起家國子生。

translations.literal: He began his career as a student of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He entered official life as a student of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 太尉文憲公王儉時爲祭酒，每稱勉有宰輔之量。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, Duke Wenxian Wang Jian, was then Libationer, and often said Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Duke Wenxian and Grand Marshal, was then Libationer of the university and often said that Mian had the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 射策舉高第，補西陽王國侍郎。

translations.literal: In the target-and-plan examination he achieved a high grade and was appointed Attendant of the Kingdom of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He placed at the top of the archery-and-policy examination and was appointed Attendant to the Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太學博士，鎮軍參軍，尚書殿中郎，以公事免。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Staff Member of the Suppressing Army, and Gentleman of the Palace in the Secretariat; he was dismissed on account of official business.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Staff Member of the Suppressing Army, and Gentleman of the Palace in the Secretariat, but was later dismissed over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 又除中兵郎、領軍長史。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Central Troops Officer and Chief Clerk of the Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Central Troops Officer and Chief Clerk on the staff of the Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王元長才名甚盛，嘗欲與勉相識，每託人召之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langye Wang Yuanchang had a very flourishing reputation for talent; he once wished to become acquainted with Mian and repeatedly had others summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanchang, Prince of Langye, was then at the height of his fame, and he repeatedly tried to arrange a meeting with Mian through intermediaries.

sentences.zh: 勉謂人曰：「王郎名高望促，難可輕醿衣裾。

translations.literal: Mian told someone, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one can hardly lightly wet the hem of one's robe with him."
translations.idiomatic: Mian told an acquaintance, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short-lived. One should not lightly trail in his wake."

sentences.zh: 」俄而元長及禍，時人莫不服其機鑒。

translations.literal: Before long Yuanchang met with disaster, and people of the time all submitted to his keen foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuanchang met with disaster, and everyone marveled at Mian's foresight.

sentences.zh: 初與長沙宣武王游，高祖深器賞之。

translations.literal: Early on he associated with the King of Changsha, King Xuanwu, and the High Ancestor deeply valued and appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he became close to Xiao Yi, King of Changsha and King Xuanwu, and the High Ancestor came to think highly of him.

sentences.zh: 及義兵至京邑，勉於新林謁見，高祖甚加恩禮，使管書記。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached the capital region, Mian presented himself at Xinlin; the High Ancestor greatly added favor and ceremony and had him manage documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army reached the capital, Mian presented himself at Xinlin. The High Ancestor treated him with special favor and put him in charge of records and correspondence.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，拜中書侍郎，遷建威將軍、後軍諮議參軍、本邑中正、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, he was appointed Secretariat Attendant and transferred to General Who Establishes Might, Adviser to the Rear General, Rectifier of his native district, and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Mian was appointed Secretariat Attendant and soon promoted to General Who Establishes Might, Adviser to the Rear General, Rectifier of his home district, and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自掌樞憲，多所糾舉，時論以爲稱職。

translations.literal: From the time he held the pivot of law and discipline, he impeached many cases; opinion of the time held that he was fit for his post.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held authority over legal discipline, he brought many cases to account, and public opinion held that he was thoroughly fit for the post.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，除給事黃門侍郎、尚書吏部郎，參掌大選。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, participating in the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, sharing responsibility for major appointments.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時王師北伐，候驛填委。

translations.literal: At that time the royal army marched north; courier stations were piled with dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the imperial army was campaigning in the north, and courier stations were buried under dispatches.

sentences.zh: 勉參掌軍書，劬勞夙夜，動經數旬，乃一還宅。

translations.literal: Mian participated in managing military documents, toiling from early to late; often several tens of days would pass before he returned home once.
translations.idiomatic: Mian shared responsibility for military correspondence and labored day and night. Weeks would pass before he returned home even once.

sentences.zh: 每還，羣犬驚吠。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned, the pack of dogs would bark in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he did return, the household dogs barked in alarm at the stranger.

sentences.zh: 勉歎曰：「吾憂國忘家，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Mian sighed and said, "I worry for the state and forget my home, even to this point."
translations.idiomatic: Mian sighed and said, "I have worried for the state until I have forgotten my own home—even to this point."

sentences.zh: 若吾亡後，亦是傳中一事。

translations.literal: If after my death this too will be an item in the tradition.
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, this too will be a story worth telling.

sentences.zh: 」六年，除給事中、五兵尚書，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Minister of the Five Armies, and transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Supervising Attendant and Minister of the Five Armies, and was then promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 勉居選官，彝倫有序，旣閑尺牘，兼善辭令，雖文案填積，坐客充滿，應對如流，手不停筆。

translations.literal: Mian held the post of selection officer; human relations were in order. He was already skilled in documents and also good at formal addresses. Though papers piled up and seated guests filled the room, he responded like flowing water and his hand did not stop the brush.
translations.idiomatic: As head of personnel appointments, Mian kept the hierarchy in good order. He was adept at paperwork and equally skilled at formal speech. Though documents piled up and his hall was always full of visitors, he answered with effortless fluency while his brush never stopped moving.

sentences.zh: 又該綜百氏，皆爲避諱。

translations.literal: He also mastered comprehensively the hundred schools, all of which he used for taboo avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: He had also mastered the writings of the hundred schools of thought and could draw on them all to avoid forbidden names.

sentences.zh: 常及閘入夜集，客有虞皓求詹事五官，勉正色答云：「今夕止可談風月，不宜及公事。

translations.literal: He often gathered guests after the gate closing into the night; a guest, Yu Hao, sought the Five Officials post under the Grand Tutor. Mian with stern countenance replied, "This evening we may only discuss wind and moon; it is not fitting to touch official business."
translations.idiomatic: He often entertained guests late into the night after the gates had closed. Once a guest named Yu Hao asked him about an appointment as one of the Five Officials under the Grand Tutor. Mian answered sternly, "Tonight we may speak only of poetry and the moon. Official business is out of place."

sentences.zh: 」故時人咸服其無私。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time all submitted to his lack of private interest.
translations.idiomatic: People admired him all the more for his impartiality.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍，領遊擊將軍，未拜，改領太子右衛率。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrently General of Roaming Attack; before taking up the appointment he was changed to concurrent Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrent General of Roaming Attack, but before he could assume the post he was reassigned as Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 遷左衛將軍，領太子中庶子，侍東宮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard, concurrently Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, attending the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Left Guard and concurrent Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, serving in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子尚幼，敕知宮事。

translations.literal: The Zhaoming Heir Apparent was still young; he was ordered to manage palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaoming Heir Apparent was still young, and Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 太子禮之甚重，每事詢謀。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent treated him with great respect and on every matter sought his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent treated him with great respect and consulted him on every matter.

sentences.zh: 嘗於殿內講《孝經》，臨川靖惠王、尚書令沈約備二傅，勉與國子祭酒張充爲執經，王瑩、張稷、柳憕、王暕爲侍講。

translations.literal: Once within the hall he lectured on the "Classic of Filial Piety"; the King of Linchuan, King Jinghui, and Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two tutors; Mian and Libationer of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Cong, and Wang Yan served as lecturing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in the palace hall, he lectured on the "Classic of Filial Piety." The King of Linchuan, King Jinghui, and Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two tutors; Mian and Libationer Zhang Chong held the text; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Cong, and Wang Yan served as lecturing attendants.

sentences.zh: 時選極親賢，妙盡時譽，勉陳讓數四。

translations.literal: The selection at the time reached the utmost in kinship and worth, wonderfully exhausting the reputation of the age; Mian submitted declining statements four times.
translations.idiomatic: The men chosen were the most eminent kinsmen and worthies of the day, and Mian declined the honor four times.

sentences.zh: 又與沈約書，求換侍講，詔不許，然後就焉。

translations.literal: He also wrote to Shen Yue asking to exchange for the post of lecturing attendant; an edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Shen Yue asking to take the lesser role of lecturing attendant instead, but the emperor refused, and only then did he accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 轉太子詹事，領雲騎將軍，尋加散騎常侍，遷尚書右僕射，詹事如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Cloud Cavalry; soon he was given the additional title of Regular Attendant and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Tutor as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrent General of Cloud Cavalry, soon given the additional title of Regular Attendant, and promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 又改授侍中，頻表解宮職，優詔不許。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant; he repeatedly submitted memorials resigning office, but gracious edicts did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Palace Attendant and repeatedly petitioned to resign, but the emperor's gracious edicts refused each request.

sentences.zh: 時人間喪事，多不遵禮，朝終夕殯，相尚以速。

translations.literal: At that time in people's funerals many did not follow ritual; mourning ended in the morning and encoffining came in the evening, and they vied with one another in speed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many people ignored proper funeral rites, encoffining the dead the same evening they died and competing to see who could bury fastest.

sentences.zh: 勉上疏曰：「《禮記問喪》云：『三日而後斂者，以俟其生也。

translations.literal: Mian submitted a memorial saying: "The Record of Rites, 'Questions on Mourning,' says: 'To encoffin only after three days is to await the person's return to life.'"
translations.idiomatic: Mian submitted a memorial saying: "In the Record of Rites, 'Questions on Mourning,' it says: 'To encoffin only after three days is to wait in case the person may yet live.'"

sentences.zh: 三日而不生，亦不生矣。

translations.literal: If after three days he does not live, he will not live.
translations.idiomatic: If after three days he has not revived, he will not revive.

sentences.zh: 』自頃以來，不遵斯制。

translations.literal: From recent times onward, this regulation has not been followed.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times this rule has been ignored.

sentences.zh: 送終之禮，殯以期日，潤屋豪家，乃或半晷，衣衾棺槨，以速爲榮，親戚徒隸，各念休反。

translations.literal: In the rites of seeing one off at the end, encoffining is set for a fixed day; wealthy houses with moistened roofs sometimes do it in half a day. Garments, covers, coffin, and outer coffin—taking speed as glory; kin, servants, and retainers each think of rest and return.
translations.idiomatic: Funerals are now scheduled for a fixed day, and in wealthy households the encoffining sometimes takes only half a day. Fine shrouds and coffins are prized for how quickly they can be finished. Relatives, servants, and retainers all think only of getting back to their rest.

sentences.zh: 故屬纊才畢，灰釘已具，忘狐鼠之顧步，愧燕雀之徊翔。

translations.literal: Thus as soon as the last breath is placed, lime and nails are already prepared; they forget the fox and rat's lingering steps and are ashamed before the swallows and sparrows' hovering flight.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the final breath is taken, the lime and nails are already ready. They forget how even foxes and rats pause over the dead, and they would be shamed by the swallows and sparrows that hover and hesitate.

sentences.zh: 傷情滅理，莫此爲大。

translations.literal: To wound feeling and extinguish principle—nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing does more violence to human feeling and moral principle than this.

sentences.zh: 且人子承衾之時，志懣心絕，喪事所資，悉關他手，愛憎深淺，事實難原。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a son receives the coverlet, his will is aggrieved and his heart cut off; what the funeral relies on is entirely in others' hands—the depth of love or hate is in fact hard to trace to its source.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when a son receives the death shroud, his heart is broken with grief. Everything needed for the funeral is handled by others, and it is hard to know whether their actions spring from love or from indifference.

sentences.zh: 如覘視或爽，存沒違濫，使萬有其一，怨酷已多。

translations.literal: If observation or attendance is neglected, and the living and dead are violated and confused, even if only one in ten thousand suffers this, the grievance and cruelty are already many.
translations.idiomatic: If the watching of the body is neglected or the rites for the living and the dead are confused, even if only one case in ten thousand goes wrong, the grief and injustice will be great.

sentences.zh: 豈若緩其告斂之晨，申其望生之冀。

translations.literal: How does this compare with slowing the morning of announcing encoffinement and extending the hope of return to life?
translations.idiomatic: How much better to delay the morning of encoffinement and preserve the hope that life may yet return?

sentences.zh: 請自今士庶，宜悉依古，三日大斂。

translations.literal: I request that from now on gentry and commoners should all follow the ancients and perform great encoffinement after three days.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on gentlemen and commoners alike follow the ancient practice and wait three days before encoffining the body.

sentences.zh: 如有不奉，加以糾繩。

translations.literal: If there are those who do not comply, let correction and punishment be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fail to comply should be subject to investigation and punishment.

sentences.zh: 」詔可其奏。

translations.literal: An edict approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋授宣惠將軍，置佐史，侍中、僕射如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Proclaims Favor, with staff officers established; Palace Attendant and Vice Director as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed General Who Proclaims Favor with a full staff, while retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 又除尚書僕射、中衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 勉以舊恩，越升重位，盡心奉上，知無不爲。

translations.literal: Mian, by reason of old favor, was promoted beyond his rank to a heavy post; he devoted his heart in serving above and there was nothing he knew that he did not do.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his long service, Mian was promoted beyond the usual measure to high office. He devoted himself wholly to the throne and left nothing undone.

sentences.zh: 爰自小選，迄於此職，常參掌衡石，甚得士心。

translations.literal: From the time of minor selection until this post, he constantly participated in holding the balance and stone, and greatly won the hearts of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: From his early work in personnel selection to this highest post, he had long held the scales of appointment, and he won the deep respect of the scholarly class.

sentences.zh: 禁省中事，未嘗漏泄。

translations.literal: Matters within the forbidden precincts, he never leaked.
translations.idiomatic: He never disclosed a single matter from within the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 每有表奏，輒焚藳草。

translations.literal: Whenever he had memorials submitted, he always burned the draft manuscripts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he drafted a memorial, he burned the working copy afterward.

sentences.zh: 博通經史，多識前載。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in the classics and histories and knew much of earlier records.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply learned in the classics and histories and knew a great deal of earlier historical writing.

sentences.zh: 朝儀國典，婚冠吉凶，勉皆預圖議。

translations.literal: Court ceremonies, state institutions, marriage and capping, auspicious and inauspicious rites — Mian all participated in planning and discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Mian took part in drafting and deliberating on court ritual, state institutions, marriage and capping ceremonies, and rites of mourning and celebration.

sentences.zh: 普通六年，上修五禮表曰：

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Putong, he submitted a memorial on revising the Five Rites, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Putong era, Mian submitted a memorial on the revision of the Five Rites, which read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞「立天之道，曰陰與陽；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: "To establish the Way of Heaven is to name yin and yang;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard it said: "To establish the Way of Heaven is to set forth yin and yang;

sentences.zh: 立人之道，曰仁與義。

translations.literal: to establish the Way of Humanity is to name benevolence and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: and to establish the Way of Humanity is to set forth benevolence and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」故稱「導之以德，齊之以禮」。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "Guide them with virtue, regulate them with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Lead the people with virtue, and harmonize them with ritual."

sentences.zh: 夫禮所以安上治民，弘風訓俗，經國家，利後嗣者也。

translations.literal: Now ritual is what settles superiors, governs the people, spreads custom, instructs society, orders the state, and benefits posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is what steadies those above, governs the people, shapes custom, educates society, sustains the state, and brings benefit to future generations.

sentences.zh: 唐虞三代，咸必由之。

translations.literal: Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties all necessarily followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The eras of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties all relied upon it without exception.

sentences.zh: 在乎有周，憲章尤備，因殷革夏，損益可知。

translations.literal: In the Zhou era, constitutional models were especially complete; building on Yin and reforming Xia, additions and subtractions can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou, the constitutional order was especially complete; inheriting from Yin and reforming Xia, its additions and revisions can still be traced.

sentences.zh: 雖復經禮三百，曲禮三千，經文三百，威儀三千，其大歸有五，卽宗伯所掌典禮：吉爲上，凶次之，賓次之，軍次之，嘉爲下也。

translations.literal: Although there were again three hundred canonical rites, three thousand detailed rites, three hundred canonical texts, and three thousand rules of bearing, their great categories number five — namely the canonical rites administered by the Minister of Rites: auspicious rites rank first, inauspicious rites next, guest rites next, military rites next, and celebratory rites last.
translations.idiomatic: Though tradition speaks of three hundred canonical rites, three thousand detailed rites, three hundred canonical passages, and three thousand rules of deportment, the great divisions are five — the ritual canon overseen by the Minister of Rites: auspicious rites first, inauspicious rites second, guest rites third, military rites fourth, and celebratory rites last.

sentences.zh: 故祠祭不以禮，則不齊不莊；

translations.literal: Therefore if sacrificial offerings are not conducted according to ritual, then there is neither order nor dignity;
translations.idiomatic: If sacrifice is not performed according to ritual, worship becomes disorderly and undignified;

sentences.zh: 喪紀不以禮，則背死忘生者衆；

translations.literal: if mourning regulations are not according to ritual, then those who turn their backs on the dead and forget the living are many;
translations.idiomatic: if mourning is not governed by ritual, many will abandon the dead and neglect the living;

sentences.zh: 賓客不以禮，則朝覲失其儀；

translations.literal: if guests are not treated according to ritual, then court audiences lose their proper form;
translations.idiomatic: if the reception of guests is not regulated by ritual, audiences at court lose their proper order;

sentences.zh: 軍旅不以禮，則致亂于師律；

translations.literal: if armies are not governed according to ritual, then disorder is brought into military discipline;
translations.idiomatic: if armies are not governed by ritual, military discipline falls into chaos;

sentences.zh: 冠婚不以禮，則男女失其時。

translations.literal: if capping and marriage are not according to ritual, then men and women miss their proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: if capping and marriage are not conducted according to ritual, men and women miss the proper seasons of life.

sentences.zh: 爲國修身，於斯攸急。

translations.literal: For governing the state and cultivating the person, in this matter it is most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: For ordering the state and cultivating the self, nothing is more urgent than this.

sentences.zh: 洎周室大壞，王道旣衰，官守斯文，日失其序。

translations.literal: When the Zhou house was greatly ruined and the royal way had already declined, officials who guarded this culture daily lost its order.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou house collapsed and the royal way declined, the officials charged with preserving these traditions lost their proper order day by day.

sentences.zh: 禮樂征伐，出自諸侯，《小雅》盡廢，舊章缺矣。

translations.literal: Ritual, music, campaigns, and punishments issued from the feudal lords; the "Lesser Odes of the Kingdom" were entirely abandoned, and old statutes were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual, music, war, and punishment passed from the throne to the feudal lords; the "Lesser Odes of the Kingdom" fell wholly into disuse, and the old regulations were lost.

sentences.zh: 是以韓宣適魯，知周公之德；

translations.literal: Therefore when Han Xuan went to Lu, he knew the virtue of the Duke of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Han Xuan of Jin visited Lu, he came to understand the virtue of the Duke of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 叔侯在晉，辨郊勞之儀。

translations.literal: Shu Hou was in Jin and distinguished the rites of suburban welcome.
translations.idiomatic: and Shu Hou, serving in Jin, was able to explain the rites of suburban welcome.

sentences.zh: 戰國從橫，政教愈泯；

translations.literal: In the Warring States era of vertical and horizontal alliances, government and teaching grew ever more extinguished;
translations.idiomatic: In the Warring States period of shifting alliances, government and moral instruction sank ever deeper into obscurity;

sentences.zh: 暴秦滅學，掃地無餘。

translations.literal: Violent Qin destroyed learning, sweeping the ground and leaving nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Then tyrannical Qin suppressed learning and swept the ground bare, leaving nothing behind.

sentences.zh: 漢氏鬱興，日不暇給，猶命叔孫于外野，方知帝王之爲貴。

translations.literal: The Han dynasty flourished abundantly, with days not enough to supply its needs; still it ordered Shusun in the outer wilds, and only then knew how precious being emperor and king was.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han rose in splendor, its affairs were so pressing that each day left no spare moment; yet the court still had to summon Shusun Tong from the wilderness to devise rites, and only then did men understand how precious imperial dignity truly was.

sentences.zh: 末葉紛綸，遞有興毀，或以武功銳志，或好黃老之言，禮義之式，於焉中止。

translations.literal: In the late branches, affairs were tangled, successively rising and falling; some were sharp in military achievement, some favored the words of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi — the forms of ritual and righteousness thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the later generations of Han, affairs grew ever more tangled, with one dynasty rising as another fell; some rulers pursued military glory with single-minded zeal, others favored the teachings of Huang-Lao — and the forms of ritual and righteousness came to a halt.

sentences.zh: 及東京曹褒，南宮制述，集其散略，百有餘篇，雖寫以尺簡，而終闕平奏。

translations.literal: By the Eastern Capital, Cao Bao formulated and compiled at the Southern Palace, gathering scattered outlines into more than a hundred pieces; though written on foot-long slips, in the end they lacked completion and submission.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital, Cao Bao compiled ritual texts at the Southern Palace, gathering scattered materials into more than a hundred chapters; though copied onto bamboo slips, the work was never brought to completion and formally submitted.

sentences.zh: 其後兵革相尋，異端互起，章句旣淪，俎豆斯輟。

translations.literal: Afterward warfare followed in succession, heterodox teachings rose one after another, commentarial passages sank away, and sacrificial vessels ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After that, war followed upon war, heterodox teachings multiplied, classical commentaries sank into oblivion, and sacrificial vessels fell silent.

sentences.zh: 方領矩步之容，事滅於旌鼓；

translations.literal: The bearing of square collars and measured steps perished amid banners and drums;
translations.idiomatic: The dignified bearing of square collars and measured steps vanished in the clash of banners and drums;

sentences.zh: 蘭臺石室之文，用盡於帷蓋。

translations.literal: The texts of the Orchid Pavilion and Stone Chamber were exhausted for tent canopies.
translations.idiomatic: and the texts preserved in the Orchid Terrace and Stone Chamber were consumed to make tent covers.

sentences.zh: 至乎晉初，爰定新禮，荀顗制之於前，摯虞刪之於末。

translations.literal: Reaching the beginning of Jin, then the new rites were fixed — Xun Yi formulated them at the start, Zhi Yu edited them at the end.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jin, a new ritual code was established: Xun Yi drafted it at the outset, and Zhi Yu revised it at the end.

sentences.zh: 旣而中原喪亂，罕有所遺；

translations.literal: Soon the Central Plains fell into disorder, and little was left behind;
translations.idiomatic: But when the Central Plains were overrun by chaos, little of it survived;

sentences.zh: 江左草創，因循而已。

translations.literal: In the southeast, it was newly established, and they merely followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: in the southeast the dynasty was newly founded, and men could do no more than follow old precedent.

sentences.zh: 𨤸革之風，是則未暇。

translations.literal: The winds of reform and innovation — for that they had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: As for the spirit of reform and innovation, there was no time for it at all.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下睿明啓運，先天改物，撥亂惟武，經世以文。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, wise and bright, inaugurated the destiny, changed things before Heaven, quelled disorder through martial virtue, and ordered the age through culture.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, wise and discerning, has inaugurated a new age, transformed the realm in accord with Heaven's mandate, quelled disorder through martial power, and governed the world through culture.

sentences.zh: 作樂在乎功成，制禮弘於業定。

translations.literal: Making music lies in accomplishing merit; instituting ritual is magnified when the enterprise is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Music is made when merit is achieved; ritual is established in full when the great enterprise is secure.

sentences.zh: 光啓二學，皇枝等於貴遊；

translations.literal: You opened two academies, placing imperial branches on a par with noble scions;
translations.idiomatic: You opened two imperial academies, placing imperial clansmen on equal footing with the sons of the nobility;

sentences.zh: 辟茲五館，草萊升以好爵。

translations.literal: You established these five halls, so men from humble fields rose to fine rank.
translations.idiomatic: and established these five halls of learning, so that men from humble fields might rise to honorable office.

sentences.zh: 爰自受命，迄于告成，盛德形容備矣，天下能事畢矣。

translations.literal: From accepting the mandate until announcing completion, your abundant virtue has been fully described, and all the world could do is done.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment you received the mandate until the present completion of your work, your great virtue has been fully realized, and every task the realm could undertake has been accomplished.

sentences.zh: 明明穆穆，無德而稱焉。

translations.literal: Bright and dignified, there are no words adequate to praise your virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Bright in wisdom and dignified in bearing, your virtue exceeds what any words can adequately praise.

sentences.zh: 至若玄符靈貺之祥，浮溟機山之賮，固亦日書左史，副在司存，今可得而略也。

translations.literal: As for auspicious signs of mysterious talismans and spiritual blessings, tribute from distant seas and Mount Jishan — these too are daily recorded by the left scribe and duplicated in the keeping offices; now they may be briefly noted.
translations.idiomatic: As for the auspicious signs of mystical talismans and divine blessings, and the tribute brought from distant seas and Mount Jishan — these too are recorded daily by the court scribes and preserved in the archives; they may be passed over briefly here.

sentences.zh: 是以命彼羣才，搜甘泉之法；

translations.literal: Therefore you ordered those many talents to search out the methods of Ganquan;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Your Majesty summoned many men of talent to search out the ritual precedents of Ganquan;

sentences.zh: 延茲碩學，闡曲臺之儀。

translations.literal: and invited these eminent scholars to expound the rites of Qutai Platform.
translations.idiomatic: and invited eminent scholars to expound the rites compiled at the Qutai Platform.

sentences.zh: 淄上淹中之儒，連蹤繼軌；

translations.literal: Confucian scholars of Zi River and Yanzhong followed one after another on the same path;
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars from Linzi and the Yanzhong academy came in an unbroken stream;

sentences.zh: 負笈懷鈆之彥，匪旦伊夕。

translations.literal: Men of talent bearing book-chests and carrying writing styli came not merely overnight.
translations.idiomatic: and learned men bearing book-chests and writing tablets arrived not in a day or a night alone.

sentences.zh: 諒以化穆三雍，人從五典，秩宗之教，勃焉以興。

translations.literal: Surely through transforming the Three Yong, people followed the Five Classics — the teachings of the Minister of Rites vigorously arose.
translations.idiomatic: Surely through the civilizing influence of the Three Yong academies, the people were brought into accord with the Five Classics, and the teachings overseen by the Minister of Rites vigorously revived.

sentences.zh: 伏尋所定五禮，起齊永明三年，太子步兵校尉伏曼容表求制一代禮樂，于時參議置新舊學士十人，止修五禮，諮稟衛將軍丹陽尹王儉，學士亦分住郡中，製作歷年，猶未克就。

translations.literal: I humbly examine the fixed Five Rites: they began in the third year of Yongming of Qi, when the Crown Prince's Infantry Commandant Fu Manrong submitted a memorial requesting the compilation of ritual and music for one generation. At that time it was deliberated to appoint ten old and new academicians, restricting the work to the Five Rites, with consultation and reporting to General of the Guard and Intendant of Danyang Wang Jian. The academicians also dispersed to reside in various commanderies. Production continued for years, yet it was still not completed.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly review the history of the Five Rites now completed: the project began in the third year of Yongming under Qi, when Fu Manrong, Infantry Commandant to the Crown Prince, submitted a memorial requesting the compilation of ritual and music for the age. At that time the court deliberated appointing ten senior and junior academicians to work exclusively on the Five Rites, reporting to Wang Jian, General of the Guard and Intendant of Danyang. The academicians were also dispersed to various commanderies. Years of work passed, yet the project remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 及文憲薨殂，遺文散逸，後又以事付國子祭酒何胤，經涉九載，猶復未畢。

translations.literal: When Wen Xian died, his surviving texts were scattered and lost. Later the task was again entrusted to Director of the Imperial Academy He Yin; nine years passed, and still it was not finished.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian, posthumously titled Wen Xian, died, his surviving manuscripts were scattered and lost. The task was later entrusted to He Yin, Director of the Imperial Academy; nine more years passed, and the work was still incomplete.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，胤還東山，齊明帝敕委尚書令徐孝嗣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin returned to East Mountain, and Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that the matter be entrusted to Director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin retired to East Mountain, and Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that the project be entrusted to Xu Xiaosi, Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 舊事本末，隨在南第。

translations.literal: The beginning and end of the old affair followed him to the Southern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: The original materials, with their full history, were kept at his Southern Residence.

sentences.zh: 永元中，孝嗣於此遇禍，又多零落。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era, Xiaosi met calamity there, and much was again scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongyuan era, Xu Xiaosi met with disaster there, and much of the material was again lost.

sentences.zh: 當時鳩斂所餘，權付尚書左丞蔡仲熊、驍騎將軍何佟之，共掌其事。

translations.literal: What remained from the collection at that time was provisionally entrusted to Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Cai Zhongxiong and General of Valiant Cavalry He Tongzhi, who jointly managed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: What remained from the earlier collection was provisionally entrusted to Cai Zhongxiong, Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, and He Tongzhi, General of Valiant Cavalry, who jointly oversaw the work.

sentences.zh: 時修禮局住在國子學中門外，東昏之代，頻有軍火，其所散失，又逾太半。

translations.literal: At that time the ritual revision bureau was located outside the middle gate of the Imperial Academy. In the reign of Emperor Hun, there were repeated military fires; what was scattered and lost again exceeded more than half.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual revision bureau was then housed outside the middle gate of the Imperial Academy. During the reign of Emperor Hun, repeated military fires broke out, and more than half of what remained was again lost.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，佟之啓審省置之宜，敕使外詳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian, Tongzhi submitted a memorial examining whether it was appropriate to reduce or retain the bureau; an edict ordered the outer offices to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian, He Tongzhi submitted a memorial on whether the bureau should be retained or abolished, and an edict ordered the outer offices to deliberate the matter.

sentences.zh: 時尚書參詳，以天地初革，庶務權輿，宜俟隆平，徐議刪撰。

translations.literal: At that time the Secretariat deliberated in detail, holding that Heaven and Earth had just been transformed, and numerous affairs were in their beginning; it was appropriate to wait for great peace and then slowly discuss editing and compilation.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat then deliberated and concluded that, with the realm newly transformed and every branch of government still in its infancy, it would be best to wait until peace was fully established before proceeding with revision and compilation.

sentences.zh: 欲且省禮局，並還尚書儀曹。

translations.literal: They wished temporarily to reduce the ritual bureau and return its functions altogether to the Rites Section of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed temporarily abolishing the ritual bureau and returning its functions to the Rites Section of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔旨云：「禮壞樂缺，故國異家殊，實宜以時修定，以爲永准。

translations.literal: The edict stated: "Ritual is ruined and music is lacking; therefore states differ and families vary. It is truly appropriate to revise and fix them in timely fashion, making them an eternal standard.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial edict read: "Ritual has fallen into ruin and music into neglect; that is why every state and every house follows different customs. The rites should indeed be revised and fixed in timely fashion, to serve as a permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 但頃之修撰，以情取人，不以學進；

translations.literal: But in recent editing and compilation, people were chosen by personal favor, not advanced by learning;
translations.idiomatic: But in recent compilations, men were chosen through personal favor rather than scholarly merit;

sentences.zh: 其掌知者，以貴總一，不以稽古，所以歷年不就，有名無實。

translations.literal: those in charge were unified by rank, not by investigation of antiquity. Therefore years passed without completion — there was a name but no substance.
translations.idiomatic: those placed in charge were selected for rank rather than knowledge of antiquity. That is why years passed without completion, and the project had a name but no substance.

sentences.zh: 此旣經國所先，外可議其人，人定，便卽撰次。

translations.literal: Since this is what ordering the state puts first, the outer offices may discuss the personnel; once the men are fixed, then immediately compile and arrange."
translations.idiomatic: Since this is a matter of first importance to the ordering of the state, the outer offices should nominate suitable men; once the personnel are settled, compilation should begin at once."

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書僕射沈約等參議，請五禮各置舊學士一人，人各自舉學士二人，相助抄撰。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Director of the Secretariat Shen Yue and others deliberated and requested that for each of the Five Rites one senior academician be appointed, each man himself recommending two academicians to assist in copying and compiling.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shen Yue, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and others deliberated and proposed that each of the Five Rites should have one senior academician appointed, each of whom would in turn recommend two academicians to assist in copying and compiling.

sentences.zh: 其中有疑者，依前漢石渠、後漢白虎，隨源以聞，請旨斷決。

translations.literal: Where there were doubts, following the precedents of Shiqu in Former Han and Baihu in Later Han, they were reported according to source for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Where doubts arose, following the precedent of the Shiqu and Baihu conferences of Han, the matter would be reported with citations and submitted for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 乃以舊學士右軍記室參軍明山賓掌吉禮，中軍騎兵參軍嚴植之掌凶禮，中軍田曹行參軍兼太常丞賀蒨掌賓禮，征虜記室參軍陸璉掌軍禮，右軍參軍司馬裴掌嘉禮，尚書左丞何佟之總參其事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the senior academician Ming Shanbin, Recorder of the Right Army Staff, was put in charge of auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Commandant of the Central Army, was put in charge of inauspicious rites; He Qian, Acting Army Field Commandant of the Central Army and concurrently Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was put in charge of guest rites; Lu Lian, Recorder of the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was put in charge of military rites; Sima Pei, Army Staff Officer of the Right Army, was put in charge of celebratory rites; and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat He Tongzhi was given overall participation in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Shanbin, senior academician and Recorder of the Right Army Staff, was placed in charge of auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Commandant of the Central Army, of inauspicious rites; He Qian, Acting Field Commandant of the Central Army and concurrently Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, of guest rites; Lu Lian, Recorder of the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, of military rites; Sima Pei, Staff Officer of the Right Army, of celebratory rites; and He Tongzhi, Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, was given overall supervision of the project.

sentences.zh: 佟之亡後，以鎮北諮議參軍伏暅代之。

translations.literal: After Tongzhi died, Fu Xiong, Advisory Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the North, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After He Tongzhi died, Fu Xiong, Advisory Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the North, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 後又以暅代嚴植之掌凶禮。

translations.literal: Later Xiong also replaced Yan Zhizhi in charge of inauspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fu Xiong also replaced Yan Zhizhi as overseer of inauspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 暅尋遷官，以《五經》博士繆昭掌凶禮。

translations.literal: Xiong soon transferred to another post, and Erudite of the Five Classics Miao Zhao was put in charge of inauspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xiong was soon transferred to another post, and Miao Zhao, Erudite of the "Five Classics," was placed in charge of inauspicious rites.

sentences.zh: 復以禮儀深廣，記載殘缺，宜須博論，共盡其致，更使鎮軍將軍丹陽尹沈約、太常卿張充及臣三人同參厥務。

translations.literal: Again, because ritual propriety was deep and broad and the records were fragmentary and incomplete, broad discussion was needed so that all might exhaust its meaning. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang; Zhang Chong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and your subject, three men, were further ordered jointly to participate in the task.
translations.idiomatic: Because ritual propriety was vast in scope and the surviving records were fragmentary, broad deliberation was needed to exhaust its full meaning. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army and Intendant of Danyang; Zhang Chong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and your subject — the three of us — were further appointed jointly to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 臣又奉別敕，總知其事。

translations.literal: Your subject also received a separate edict to oversee the affair in general.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also received a separate edict placing me in overall charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 末又使中書侍郎周捨、庾於陵二人復豫參知。

translations.literal: Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yuan Yuling were again ordered to participate in consultation and knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yuan Yuling were also appointed to take part in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 若有疑義，所掌學士當職先立議，通諮五禮舊學士及參知，各言同異，條牒啓聞，決之制旨。

translations.literal: If there were doubtful points, the academician in charge of the duty would first establish a proposal, consult broadly with the senior academicians of the Five Rites and the participants in consultation, each stating agreement or difference; the items would be submitted in memorial for decision by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: When a doubtful point arose, the academician responsible would first draft a proposal, consult the senior academicians of the Five Rites and the other participants, record each man's agreement or dissent, submit the matter in memorial, and await the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 疑事旣多，歲時又積，制旨裁斷，其數不少。

translations.literal: Doubtful matters were already many, and years also accumulated; imperial edicts deciding them were not a few in number.
translations.idiomatic: The doubtful points were many, and the years accumulated; the number of imperial decisions handed down was considerable.

sentences.zh: 莫不網羅經誥，玉振金聲，義貫幽微，理入神契。

translations.literal: None failed to gather the canonical teachings, jade vibrating and gold sounding; meaning penetrated the subtle, and principle entered divine accord.
translations.idiomatic: Every decision drew upon the canonical texts with the resonance of jade and gold; meaning reached into the subtlest depths, and principle attained a harmony that seemed almost divine.

sentences.zh: 前儒所不釋，後學所未聞。

translations.literal: What former Confucians did not explain, later students had not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Points that earlier scholars had left unresolved were settled here; matters that later students had never heard explained were made clear.

sentences.zh: 凡諸奏決，皆載篇首，具列聖旨，爲不刊之則。

translations.literal: All memorial decisions were recorded at the head of each section, fully listing the sage intent, forming an unalterable standard.
translations.idiomatic: Every decision submitted and approved was recorded at the head of the relevant section, with the imperial intent fully set forth, to serve as an immutable standard.

sentences.zh: 洪規盛範，冠絕百王；

translations.literal: Grand regulations and flourishing models surpass all hundred kings;
translations.idiomatic: These grand regulations and magnificent models surpass those of all the kings of old;

sentences.zh: 茂實英聲，方垂千載。

translations.literal: abundant substance and outstanding renown will be handed down for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: their substance is rich and their renown splendid, and they will be handed down for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 寧孝宣之能擬，豈孝章之足云。

translations.literal: Can even Emperor Xiaoxuan be compared? How could Emperor Xiaozhang suffice to mention?
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Xuan of Han could scarcely be compared with this achievement — to say nothing of Emperor Zhang.

sentences.zh: 五禮之職，事有繁簡，及其列畢，不得同時。

translations.literal: The duties of the Five Rites had affairs both complex and simple; when each was arranged and completed, they could not all be finished at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: The work of the Five Rites varied in complexity, and the sections were completed at different times rather than all at once.

sentences.zh: 《嘉禮儀注》以天監六年五月七日上尚書，合十有二秩，一百一十六卷，五百三十六條；

translations.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Celebratory Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventh day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling twelve sections, one hundred sixteen scrolls, and five hundred thirty-six articles;
translations.idiomatic: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Celebratory Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventh day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, comprising twelve sections, one hundred sixteen scrolls, and five hundred thirty-six articles;

sentences.zh: 《賓禮儀注》以天監六年五月二十日上尚書，合十有七秩，一百三十三卷，五百四十五條；

translations.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Guest Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the twentieth day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianjian, totaling seventeen sections, one hundred thirty-three scrolls, and five hundred forty-five articles;
translations.idiomatic: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Guest Rites" was submitted on the twentieth day of the fifth month of the same year, comprising seventeen sections, one hundred thirty-three scrolls, and five hundred forty-five articles;

sentences.zh: 《軍禮儀注》以天監九年十月二十九日上尚書，合十有八秩，一百八十九卷，二百四十條；

translations.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Military Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Tianjian, totaling eighteen sections, one hundred eighty-nine scrolls, and two hundred forty articles;
translations.idiomatic: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Military Rites" was submitted on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Tianjian, comprising eighteen sections, one hundred eighty-nine scrolls, and two hundred forty articles;

sentences.zh: 《吉禮儀注》以天監十一年十一月十日上尚書，合二十有六秩，二百二十四卷，一千五條；

translations.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Auspicious Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling twenty-six sections, two hundred twenty-four scrolls, and one thousand five articles;
translations.idiomatic: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Auspicious Rites" was submitted on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, comprising twenty-six sections, two hundred twenty-four scrolls, and one thousand five articles;

sentences.zh: 《凶禮儀注》以天監十一年十一月十七日上尚書，合四十有七秩，五百一十四卷，五千六百九十三條：大凡一百二十秩，一千一百七十六卷，八千一十九條。

translations.literal: "Regulations and Commentaries on Inauspicious Rites" was submitted to the Secretariat on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Tianjian, totaling forty-seven sections, five hundred fourteen scrolls, and five thousand six hundred ninety-three articles: in all one hundred twenty sections, one thousand one hundred seventy-six scrolls, and eight thousand nineteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: The "Regulations and Commentaries on Inauspicious Rites" was submitted on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month of the same year, comprising forty-seven sections, five hundred fourteen scrolls, and five thousand six hundred ninety-three articles — in all one hundred twenty sections, one thousand one hundred seventy-six scrolls, and eight thousand nineteen articles.

sentences.zh: 又列副秘閣及《五經》典書各一通，繕寫校定，以普通五年二月始獲洗畢。

translations.literal: Copies were also arranged for the Secret Archive and for the Keeper of the "Five Classics," one set each; copying, writing, and collation were completed, and in the second month of the fifth year of Putong they were finally finished in clean form.
translations.idiomatic: Duplicate sets were also prepared for the Secret Archive and for the Keeper of the "Five Classics," one copy each. Copying and collation were completed, and fair copies were finally finished in the second month of the fifth year of Putong.

sentences.zh: 竊以撰正履禮，歷代罕就，皇明在運，厥功克成。

translations.literal: I venture to consider that compiling, correcting, and practicing ritual has rarely been accomplished in successive generations; now under imperial brightness the age is in motion, and this merit has been able to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to observe that compiling and establishing ritual has rarely been brought to completion in any age; yet under Your Majesty's enlightened reign this great work has at last been achieved.

sentences.zh: 周代三千，舉其盈數；

translations.literal: The Zhou era had three thousand, taking its full number;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou spoke of three thousand rites, reaching the full traditional count;

sentences.zh: 今之八千，隨事附益。

translations.literal: today's eight thousand follow affairs in addition and increase.
translations.idiomatic: today's eight thousand articles reflect additions made as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 質文相變，故其數兼倍，猶如八卦之爻，因而重之，錯綜成六十四也。

translations.literal: Substance and form change each other; therefore the number is doubled — just like the lines of the eight trigrams, which are then doubled and interwoven to form sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: As substance and form change with the times, the number has naturally doubled — just as the lines of the eight trigrams, when doubled and interwoven, become sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 昔文武二王，所以綱紀周室，君臨天下，公旦修之，以致太平龍鳳之瑞。

translations.literal: Formerly the two kings Wen and Wu thereby regulated the Zhou house, ruled over all under Heaven; the Duke of Zhou refined it, thereby attaining the auspicious signs of peace with dragon and phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Kings Wen and Wu used ritual to order the Zhou house and rule the realm; the Duke of Zhou refined it, bringing about the age of peace marked by the auspicious appearances of dragon and phoenix.

sentences.zh: 自斯厥後，甫備茲日。

translations.literal: From that time until now, only on this day has it been fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: From that age until now, only on this day has such a work been fully completed.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「其有繼周，雖百世可知。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "If there is one to succeed Zhou, even after a hundred generations it can be known."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "If there is one to succeed Zhou, even after a hundred generations its way may be foreknown."

sentences.zh: 」豈所謂齊功比美者歟！

translations.literal: Is this not what is called equal in achievement and comparable in beauty!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not what is meant by matching Zhou in achievement and in splendor!

sentences.zh: 臣以庸識，謬司其任，淹留歷稔，允當斯責；

translations.literal: Your subject, with mediocre understanding, was wrongly entrusted with this duty; lingering through accumulated years, I have truly borne this responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, with my mediocre understanding, was undeservedly entrusted with this charge; I have lingered in the post for many years and have truly borne its weight.

sentences.zh: 兼勒成之初，未遑表上，實由才輕務廣，思力不周，永言慚惕，無忘寤寐。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning when completion was achieved, I had no leisure to submit a memorial — truly because talent was slight and tasks were broad, thought and strength were not comprehensive. I always speak with shame and caution, never forgetting waking or sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was first completed, I had not yet submitted this memorial, truly because my ability was slight and the task vast, and my thought and strength were not equal to it. I remain ashamed and apprehensive, and the matter has never left my mind, waking or sleeping.

sentences.zh: 自今春輿駕將親六師，搜尋軍禮，閱其條章，靡不該備。

translations.literal: Since this spring the imperial carriage will personally lead the Six Armies; searching through military rites and examining their articles and regulations, none are not comprehensive and complete.
translations.idiomatic: This spring, as Your Majesty's carriage prepares to lead the armies in person, I searched through the military rites and reviewed their articles and regulations — all are comprehensive and complete.

sentences.zh: 所謂郁郁文哉，煥乎洋溢，信可以懸諸日月，頒之天下者矣。

translations.literal: What is called richly cultured indeed, brilliantly overflowing — truly it can be suspended beside sun and moon and promulgated throughout all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Truly it is richly cultured and brilliantly complete — a work that may be displayed beside sun and moon and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 愚心喜抃，彌思陳述；

translations.literal: My foolish heart rejoices and claps hands; I all the more wish to set forth and state;
translations.idiomatic: My humble heart rejoices at this achievement, and I am all the more moved to report it;

sentences.zh: 兼前後聯官，一時皆逝，臣雖倖存，耄已將及，慮皇世大典，遂闕騰奏，不任下情，輒具載撰修始末，并職掌人、所成卷秩、條目之數，謹拜表以聞。

translations.literal: Moreover, the officials connected before and after all passed away at one time; though your subject survives by fortune, old age is already approaching. Fearing that the great canon of the imperial age would thus lack a submitted memorial, unable to bear my lower feelings, I have fully recorded the beginning and end of compilation and revision, together with the persons in charge, the scroll sections completed, and the number of articles, and respectfully bow with this memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the officials who served before and after me have all passed away; though I alone survive, old age is already upon me. Fearing that this great canon of the imperial age might never be formally reported, and unable to suppress my earnest feeling, I have set forth in full the history of the compilation, the officials in charge, and the number of scrolls and articles completed, and respectfully submit this memorial for Your Majesty's notice.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「經禮大備，政典載弘，今詔有司，案以行事也。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The canonical rites are greatly complete, and the governmental canon is broadly enlarged. Now we order the responsible offices to follow them in conducting affairs."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "The canonical rites are now fully complete, and the governmental canon greatly enriched. Let the responsible offices implement them in practice."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「勉表如此。

translations.literal: " Another edict stated: "Mian's memorial is as this."
translations.idiomatic: " Another edict read: "Mian's memorial is as stated."

sentences.zh: 因革允𨤸，憲章孔備，功成業定，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Changing and keeping what is suitable, statutes and patterns fully complete; achievement accomplished and enterprise settled — herein it lies.
translations.idiomatic: Reform and preservation duly balanced, statutes and patterns fully complete; the work accomplished and the enterprise settled — all is fulfilled here.

sentences.zh: 可以光被八表，施諸百代，俾萬世之下，知斯文在斯。

translations.literal: It can radiate to the eight directions, be applied through a hundred generations, so that beneath ten thousand generations men may know that this culture is here.
translations.idiomatic: It may shine across the eight directions and be handed down through a hundred generations, so that for ten thousand years to come men may know that this civilization endures here.

sentences.zh: 主者其按以遵行，勿有失墜。

translations.literal: Let those in charge examine it and follow it; let nothing be lost or neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible officials review it and carry it out; let nothing be allowed to fall away.

sentences.zh: 」尋加中書令，給親信二十人。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Director of the Secretariat and granted twenty personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was further appointed Director of the Secretariat and granted twenty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 勉以疾自陳，求解內任。

translations.literal: Mian, citing illness, submitted a memorial requesting release from inner-court duties.
translations.idiomatic: Mian pleaded illness in a memorial, asking to be relieved of his duties within the palace.

sentences.zh: 詔不許，乃令停下省，三日一朝，有事遣主書論決。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it; instead he was ordered to remain at the Secretariat but cease daily attendance, coming to court every three days, with matters sent to chief clerks for discussion and decision.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused; instead he was told to stay at the Secretariat without daily attendance, appearing at court every three days while routine business was referred to chief clerks for deliberation and decision.

sentences.zh: 腳疾轉劇，久闕朝覲，固陳求解，詔乃賚假，須疾差還省。

translations.literal: His foot ailment grew worse; having long missed court audience, he repeatedly requested release; an edict then granted him leave, requiring return to the Secretariat once the illness improved.
translations.idiomatic: His foot ailment worsened, and after long absence from court he again pressed to resign; the emperor then granted him leave, with orders to return to office once he recovered.

sentences.zh: 勉雖居顯位，不營產業，家無蓄積，俸祿分贍親族之窮乏者。

translations.literal: Though Mian held a prominent position, he did not pursue property; his household had no savings, and his salary was divided to support needy relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Though Mian held high office, he did not build up an estate; his household kept no reserves, and he divided his salary to support impoverished kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 門人故舊或從容致言。

translations.literal: Students and old friends sometimes spoke to him at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Students and old friends would sometimes raise the matter with him in easy conversation.

sentences.zh: 勉乃答曰：「人遺子孫以財，我遺之以清白。

translations.literal: Mian replied: "Others leave their descendants wealth; I leave them integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Mian answered: "People leave their children wealth; I leave them a name for integrity.

sentences.zh: 子孫才也，則自致輜軿；

translations.literal: If one's descendants have talent, they will obtain covered carriages on their own;
translations.idiomatic: If a man's sons have ability, they will win fine carriages for themselves;

sentences.zh: 如其不才，終爲他有。

translations.literal: if they lack talent, wealth will ultimately belong to others.
translations.idiomatic: if they lack talent, whatever wealth there is will end up in others' hands.

sentences.zh: 」嘗爲書誡其子崧曰：

translations.literal: " He once wrote a letter admonishing his son Song, saying:
