translations.idiomatic: " He once wrote a letter of admonition to his son Song, which read:

sentences.zh: 吾家世清廉，故常居貧素，至於產業之事，所未嘗言，非直不經營而已。

translations.literal: Our family has been upright through the generations and thus has always lived in plain poverty. As for matters of property, I have never even spoken of them — not merely refrained from managing them.
translations.idiomatic: Our house has been honest for generations, and so we have always lived plainly. I have never so much as spoken of property — it is not simply that I have refused to manage it.

sentences.zh: 薄躬遭逢，遂至今日，尊官厚祿，可謂備之。

translations.literal: My humble self, having met with fortune, has come to this day; high office and generous salary — one might say I possess them all.
translations.idiomatic: My humble person, favored by circumstance, has risen to where I stand today; high rank and ample stipend — you might say I have them in full.

sentences.zh: 每念叨竊若斯，豈由才致，仰藉先代風範及以福慶，故臻此耳。

translations.literal: Whenever I think how undeservedly I hold such rank, it is surely not through my own ability; I rely upon the moral bearing of earlier generations and upon accumulated blessings — that is how I have reached this.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on how unworthily I hold such eminence, I know it is not through my own merit; I owe it to the example of my forebears and to inherited good fortune — that alone has brought me here.

sentences.zh: 古人所謂「以清白遺子孫，不亦厚乎！

translations.literal: What the ancients meant by "leaving integrity to one's descendants — is that not a generous legacy!
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said, "To bequeath integrity to one's descendants — is that not the richest gift?

sentences.zh: 」又云：「遺子黃金滿籝，不如一經。

translations.literal: " It is also said: "To leave one's son a basket brimming with gold is not as good as leaving him one classic.
translations.idiomatic: " And again: "To leave a son gold enough to fill a basket is inferior to leaving him one classic.

sentences.zh: 」詳求此言，信非徒語。

translations.literal: " Reflecting carefully on these words, one finds they are truly not empty speech.
translations.idiomatic: " Consider those words closely, and you will see they are no idle sayings.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不敏，實有本志，庶得遵奉斯義，不敢墜失。

translations.literal: Though I am not clever, I truly hold to this original resolve, hoping to follow this principle and not dare let it fall away.
translations.idiomatic: I am not clever, but this has always been my aim; I mean to live by that principle and not let it slip.

sentences.zh: 所以顯貴以來，將三十載，門人故舊，亟薦便宜，或使創辟田園，或勸興立邸店，又欲舳艫運致，亦令貨殖聚斂。

translations.literal: Since I rose to eminence, nearly thirty years have passed; students and old friends have repeatedly urged expedient measures — some suggesting opening up estates and gardens, some urging the founding of inns and shops, others wishing to transport goods by boat, all recommending commercial profit and accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the nearly thirty years since I rose to prominence, students and old friends have again and again pressed practical schemes on me — some urging me to open fields and gardens, some to set up inns and shops, others to freight goods by river, all counseling trade and accumulation.

sentences.zh: 若此衆事，皆距而不納。

translations.literal: Such proposals I have all rejected and refused.
translations.idiomatic: I have turned every such proposal away.

sentences.zh: 非謂拔葵去織，且欲省息紛紜。

translations.literal: I do not mean this as pulling up melons and removing weaving; I simply wish to reduce and quiet the bustle.
translations.idiomatic: This is not the purism of pulling up melons and forbidding weaving at home; I simply want to spare myself the noise and bother.

sentences.zh: 中年聊於東田間營小園者，非在播藝，以要利入，正欲穿池種樹，少寄情賞。

translations.literal: In middle age I briefly laid out a small garden among the eastern fields — not to cultivate crops for profit, but simply to dig a pond and plant trees, giving a little scope to refined pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: In middle age I casually laid out a small garden on the eastern fields — not to farm for profit, but to dig a pond, plant trees, and find a little room for quiet delight.

sentences.zh: 又以郊際閑曠，終可爲宅，儻獲懸車致事，實欲歌哭於斯。

translations.literal: Also because the outskirts are open and spacious and could in the end serve as a dwelling — if I should obtain release from office at the age of seventy, I truly mean to sing and weep my days there.
translations.idiomatic: The suburbs are open and spacious and could serve as a home; if I should retire at seventy, I truly mean to spend my remaining days there in joy and sorrow alike.

sentences.zh: 慧日、十住等，旣應營婚，又須住止，吾清明門宅，無相容處。

translations.literal: Huiri, Shizhu, and the others must both arrange marriages and need places to live; my residence at Qingming Gate has no room to accommodate them.
translations.idiomatic: Huiri, Shizhu, and the others must marry and need places to live, yet my house at Qingming Gate has no space for them.

sentences.zh: 所以爾者，亦復有以；

translations.literal: The reason for this, moreover, has its grounds;
translations.idiomatic: There is reason for this as well;

sentences.zh: 前割西邊施宣武寺，旣失西廂，不復方幅，意亦謂此逆旅舍耳，何事須華？

translations.literal: Previously I ceded the western portion to Xuanwu Temple; having lost the west wing, the compound is no longer square and whole. I also regard it as nothing but an inn — why must it be splendid?
translations.idiomatic: I earlier gave the western wing to Xuanwu Temple; without it the house is no longer a proper square. I think of it as a roadside inn — why should it be grand?

sentences.zh: 常恨時人謂是我宅。

translations.literal: I have always resented that people of the day call it my mansion.
translations.idiomatic: I have always resented people calling it my mansion.

sentences.zh: 古往今來，豪富繼踵，高門甲第，連闥洞房，宛其死矣，定是誰室？

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, the wealthy succeed one another; grand gates and mansions, linked halls and inner chambers — when the owner is dead, whose house are they?
translations.idiomatic: From ancient times to now, the rich have followed one after another — great gates and mansions, halls linked to chambers. When the owner dies, whose house is it?

sentences.zh: 但不能不爲培塿之山，聚石移果，雜以花卉，以娛休沐，用誌性靈。

translations.literal: Yet one cannot but raise a mound of earth here and there, gather stones and transplant fruit trees, mix in flowers, to delight in days of rest, and give expression to one's inner spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Still, one cannot help raising a little hill, gathering stones, moving fruit trees, and planting flowers — to enjoy days of rest and give the spirit its due.

sentences.zh: 隨便架立，不在廣大，惟功德處，小以爲好。

translations.literal: Build whatever is convenient; vastness is not the aim — only where merit is to be done is smallness preferred.
translations.idiomatic: Build as convenience allows; size is not the point — only where good is to be done do I prefer things modest.

sentences.zh: 所以內中逼促，無復房宇。

translations.literal: That is why the interior is cramped and there is no surplus room.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the inner quarters are cramped and there is no spare room.

sentences.zh: 近營東邊兒孫二宅，乃藉十住南還之資，其中所須，猶爲不少，旣牽挽不至，又不可中塗而輟，郊間之園，遂不辦保，貨與韋黯，乃獲百金，成就兩宅，已消其半。

translations.literal: Recently I built two residences eastward for children and grandchildren, drawing on the funds Shizhu brought back from the south; what was still required was considerable. Since funds could not be raised in time, and the work could not be halted midway, I was unable to keep the suburban garden and sold it to Wei An, obtaining a hundred gold pieces; the two houses were completed, consuming half of it.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I built two houses to the east for my children and grandchildren, using the money Shizhu brought back from the south; even so, much was still needed. When further funds failed to arrive and the work could not be abandoned halfway, I could not keep the suburban garden and sold it to Wei An for a hundred gold pieces — enough to finish both houses, though half was already gone.

sentences.zh: 尋園價所得，何以至此？

translations.literal: You may wonder how the sale of the garden fetched so much.
translations.idiomatic: You may ask how the garden fetched so high a price.

sentences.zh: 由吾經始歷年，粗已成立，桃李茂密，桐竹成陰，塍陌交通，渠畎相屬，華樓迥榭，頗有臨眺之美；

translations.literal: Because I had founded it over many years and it was roughly complete: peach and plum trees dense, paulownia and bamboo casting shade, paths crossing fields, irrigation ditches linked together, elegant towers and distant pavilions with fine views for gazing afar;
translations.idiomatic: Because I had worked on it for years and it was largely finished: peaches and plums in thick leaf, paulownia and bamboo in shade, field paths crossing, irrigation channels linked, elegant towers and distant pavilions with fine views;

sentences.zh: 孤峰叢薄，不無糾紛之興。

translations.literal: solitary peaks and thickets — not without stirrings of poetic feeling.
translations.idiomatic: solitary peaks and brushy slopes — enough to stir the mind to verse.

sentences.zh: 瀆中並饒菰蔣，湖裏殊富芰蓮。

translations.literal: The channel abounds in wild rice and rushes; the lake is rich in water chestnuts and lotus.
translations.idiomatic: The ditch teemed with wild rice and rushes; the lake was rich in water chestnuts and lotus.

sentences.zh: 雖云人外，城闕密邇，韋生欲之，亦雅有情趣。

translations.literal: Though it is said to be beyond the city of men, the walls are close by; Wei wanted it, and with good reason — it had refined charm.
translations.idiomatic: Though it lay outside the city, the walls were near; Wei wanted it, and no wonder — it had real charm.

sentences.zh: 追述此事，非有吝心，蓋是筆勢所至耳。

translations.literal: In recounting this, I feel no regret or stinginess; it is simply where the pen carried me.
translations.idiomatic: I tell this story not from regret or stinginess, but because my pen ran on.

sentences.zh: 憶謝靈運《山家詩》云：「中爲天地物，今成鄙夫有。

translations.literal: I recall Xie Lingyun's "Mountain Dwelling Poem": "What was once a thing of Heaven and Earth now belongs to a common man.
translations.idiomatic: I remember Xie Lingyun's "Mountain Dwelling Poem": "What was once Heaven and Earth's now belongs to a common man.

sentences.zh: 」吾此園有之二十載矣，今爲天地物，物之與我，相校幾何哉！

translations.literal: " I have possessed this garden for twenty years; now it returns to being a thing of Heaven and Earth — between the thing and me, how great is the difference!
translations.idiomatic: " I held this garden twenty years; now it is Heaven and Earth's again — between the place and me, how great is the difference!

sentences.zh: 此吾所餘，今以分汝，營小田舍，親累旣多，理亦須此。

translations.literal: This is what remains to me; I now divide it with you to establish a small farmstead — with so many dependents in the family, it is only reasonable to need this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I have left; I now give you your share to set up a small farm — with so many mouths in the family, you need it.

sentences.zh: 且釋氏之教，以財物謂之外命；

translations.literal: Moreover, in Buddhist teaching wealth and goods are called the outer life;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Buddhist teaching calls wealth and goods the outer life;

sentences.zh: 儒典亦稱「何以聚人曰財」。

translations.literal: the Confucian classics also say, "By what do men gather together? By wealth."
translations.idiomatic: and the Confucian canon says, "By what do men gather? By wealth."

sentences.zh: 況汝曹常情，安得忘此。

translations.literal: How much more so for you — ordinary human feelings — how could you forget this?
translations.idiomatic: And you are only human — how could you ignore that?

sentences.zh: 聞汝所買姑孰田地，甚爲舄鹵，彌復何安。

translations.literal: I hear the land you bought at Gushu is very salinous and poor — how could that set my mind at ease?
translations.idiomatic: I hear the land you bought at Gushu is poor and salty — how can that comfort me?

sentences.zh: 所以如此，非物競故也。

translations.literal: My concern is not from competing over property.
translations.idiomatic: I say this not from rivalry over possessions.

sentences.zh: 雖事異寢丘，聊可髣髴。

translations.literal: Though the matter differs from sleeping on a mound, it may serve as a rough likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Though this is not the same as the mound at Qufu, it may serve in some measure.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「居家理治，可移於官。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Ordering one's household well may be transferred to office.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Good household governance can be carried into public office.

sentences.zh: 」旣已營之，宜使成立。

translations.literal: " Since you have begun it, you should bring it to completion.
translations.idiomatic: " Since you have begun, you should see it through.

sentences.zh: 進退兩亡，更貽恥笑。

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating both lost — that would only invite mockery.
translations.idiomatic: To advance and fail, or to retreat halfway — either way brings shame.

sentences.zh: 若有所收穫，汝可自分贍內外大小，宜令得所，非吾所知，又復應沾之諸女耳。

translations.literal: If there is any harvest, you may yourself distribute support to those within and without, great and small, seeing that each has what's fitting — as for details, that is not for me to know; only that the daughters entitled to a share should receive one.
translations.idiomatic: If there is a harvest, divide it yourself among the household, great and small, as each deserves — the details are yours to manage; only remember the daughters who should share in it.

sentences.zh: 汝旣居長，故有此及。

translations.literal: Since you are the eldest, I address you on this.
translations.idiomatic: Because you are the eldest, I write to you about this.

sentences.zh: 凡爲人長，殊復不易，當使中外諧緝，人無間言，先物後己，然後可貴。

translations.literal: To be the eldest in a family is truly not easy; one must keep inner and outer circles in harmony, so that no one has complaint, putting others before oneself — only then is one worthy of respect.
translations.idiomatic: To be the eldest is no easy thing: keep kin and household in harmony, leave no room for gossip, put others before yourself — only then are you worth respect.

sentences.zh: 老生云：「後其身而身先。

translations.literal: Laozi said: "Put yourself behind and you will be ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The Old Master said, "Put yourself last and you will be first.

sentences.zh: 」若能爾者，更招巨利。

translations.literal: " If you can do this, you will reap great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: " Live that way and you will gain much.

sentences.zh: 汝當自勗，見賢思齊，不宜忽略以棄日也。

translations.literal: You must urge yourself on, seeing the worthy and thinking to equal them; you must not neglect and waste your days.
translations.idiomatic: Exhort yourself: when you see the worthy, strive to match them; do not waste your days in idleness.

sentences.zh: 非徒棄日，乃是棄身，身名美惡，豈不大哉！

translations.literal: Not merely wasting days — you waste yourself; the beauty or ugliness of one's person and name — is that not momentous!
translations.idiomatic: That is not merely wasting days — it is wasting your life; the honor or disgrace of your name — is that not weighty!

sentences.zh: 可不慎歟？

translations.literal: Can one not be careful?
translations.idiomatic: Can you not be on your guard?

sentences.zh: 今之所敕，略言此意。

translations.literal: What I admonish today briefly states this intention.
translations.idiomatic: What I urge upon you now is only this in brief.

sentences.zh: 正謂爲家已來，不事資產，旣立墅舍，以乖舊業，陳其始末，無愧懷抱。

translations.literal: I mean precisely that since taking charge of the household I have not pursued assets; having now established a villa, I depart from my old practice — yet in recounting the whole course, I have nothing to reproach in my conscience.
translations.idiomatic: I mean that though I have never pursued property for the household, I have now built a villa and departed from my old way — yet in telling the whole story, my conscience is clear.

sentences.zh: 兼吾年時朽暮，心力稍殫，牽課奉公，略不克舉，其中餘暇，裁可自休。

translations.literal: Moreover I am now old and declining; my strength is largely spent. Dragged by duties to serve the state, I can barely manage; whatever leisure remains barely suffices for my own rest.
translations.idiomatic: I am old now, my strength nearly gone; bound to public duty, I can barely keep up, and what little time remains is barely enough for rest.

sentences.zh: 或復冬日之陽，夏日之陰，良辰美景，文案間隙，負杖躡屩，逍遙陋館，臨池觀魚，披林聽鳥，濁酒一杯，彈琴一曲，求數刻之暫樂，庶居常以待終，不宜復勞家間細務。

translations.literal: On winter sun or summer shade, fine days and lovely scenes, in intervals between documents — leaning on my staff, slipping on straw sandals, roaming my humble lodge, gazing at fish by the pond, listening to birds in the groves, a cup of coarse wine, a stretch upon the zither, seeking a few moments' pleasure, hoping to abide peacefully until the end — I ought not again be burdened with household minutiae.
translations.idiomatic: On a winter sun or summer shade, on fine days amid lovely scenes, in brief gaps between documents — staff in hand, sandals on my feet, wandering my humble lodge, watching fish in the pond, listening to birds in the grove, a cup of plain wine, a tune on the zither, a few moments' joy before the end — I should not be troubled again with household trifles.

sentences.zh: 汝交關旣定，此書又行，凡所資須，付給如別。

translations.literal: Your arrangements are settled, this letter goes forth; whatever is needed shall be supplied as separately indicated.
translations.idiomatic: Your affairs are settled, and with this letter everything required will be provided as listed separately.

sentences.zh: 自茲以後，吾不復言及田事，汝亦勿復與吾言之。

translations.literal: From now on I shall speak of field affairs no more; you also must not speak of them to me again.
translations.idiomatic: From now on I will not speak of the farm, and you must not speak of it to me either.

sentences.zh: 假使堯水湯旱，吾豈知如何；

translations.literal: Even if floods like Yao's or drought like Tang's should come, what would I know of it?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yao's flood or Tang's drought should come, what would I know?

sentences.zh: 若其滿庾盈箱，爾之幸遇。

translations.literal: If bins overflow and granaries brim, that is your good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If the bins are full and the granaries overflow, that is your good luck.

sentences.zh: 如斯之事，並無俟令吾知也。

translations.literal: Such matters need not await my being told.
translations.idiomatic: Matters like that need not be reported to me.

sentences.zh: 《記》云：「夫孝者，善繼人之志，善述人之事。

translations.literal: The "Record" says: "Filial piety means well continuing another's will and well carrying out another's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The "Record" says, "Filial piety is to continue another's aim well and carry on another's work well.

sentences.zh: 」今且望汝全吾此志，則無所恨矣。

translations.literal: For now I hope you will fulfill this will of mine, and then I shall have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: For now I ask only that you honor this wish of mine, and I shall have no regret.

sentences.zh: 勉第二子悱卒，痛悼甚至，不欲久廢王務，乃爲《答客喻》。

translations.literal: When Mian's second son Fei died, his grief was extreme; unwilling to long neglect state affairs, he composed "Answer to the Guest's Remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: When Mian's second son Fei died, his grief was profound; unwilling to neglect state business for long, he wrote "Answer to the Guest's Remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words read:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 普通五年春二月丁丑，余第二息晉安內史悱喪之問至焉，舉家傷悼，心情若隕。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the fifth year of Putong, on day dingchou, word came of the death of my second son Fei, Interior Secretary of Jin'an; the whole household mourned, hearts as if fallen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, fifth year of Putong, on day dingchou, word arrived that my second son Fei, Interior Secretary of Jin'an, had died; the whole household grieved, our hearts as though they had dropped from the sky.

sentences.zh: 二宮並降中使，以相慰勗，親游賓客，畢來弔問，輒慟哭失聲，悲不自已，所謂父子天性，不知涕之所從來也。

translations.literal: Both palaces sent palace envoys to console and encourage; relatives, friends, and guests all came to offer condolences. I would burst into wailing beyond control, grief unchecked — what is called the nature of father and son; I knew not whence the tears came.
translations.idiomatic: Both palaces sent envoys to comfort and encourage us; kin, friends, and guests all came to mourn. I would break into uncontrollable wailing, grief I could not restrain — the bond between father and son; I did not know where the tears came from.

sentences.zh: 於是門人慮其肆情所鐘，容致委頓，乃斂衽而進曰：「僕聞古往今來，理運之常數；

translations.literal: Then my students, fearing his abandoned emotion might waste his strength, straightened their robes and stepped forward, saying: "Your servant has heard that from antiquity to the present, the order of principle and fate follows constant patterns;
translations.idiomatic: Then his students, fearing that such unchecked grief might exhaust him, straightened their robes and came forward: "We have heard that from ancient times to the present, principle and fate follow fixed laws;

sentences.zh: 春榮秋落，氣象之定期。

translations.literal: spring glory and autumn fall are fixed seasons of the natural order.
translations.idiomatic: spring's flourishing and autumn's decline are the appointed seasons of nature.

sentences.zh: 人居其間，譬諸逆旅，生寄死歸，著於通論，是以深識之士，悠爾忘懷。

translations.literal: Men dwell between them like guests at an inn; life is lodging, death is return — so runs the common teaching; hence the deeply knowing gentleman lightly forgets and releases.
translations.idiomatic: Men live between them like travelers at an inn: life is a sojourn, death a return home — so the common teaching runs; therefore the wise man lightly lets go.

sentences.zh: 東門歸無之旨，見稱往哲；

translations.literal: The meaning of 'return without sorrow at the eastern gate' has been praised by sages of old;
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of 'no grief at the eastern gate' was praised by the sages of old;

sentences.zh: 西河喪明之過，取誚友朋。

translations.literal: the fault of mourning blindness at Xihe drew mockery from friends.
translations.idiomatic: while blinding oneself in grief at Xihe brought reproach from friends.

sentences.zh: 足下受遇於朝，任居端右，憂深責重，休戚是均，宜其遺情下流，止哀加飯，上存奉國，俯示隆家。

translations.literal: You have been favored by the court, hold the foremost post on the right, bear heavy cares and grave responsibility, sharing weal and woe alike. You ought to set aside lower emotion, stop grief and take food; above, preserve service to the state; below, display the flourishing of your house.
translations.idiomatic: You are favored by the court, hold the highest office on the right, and bear heavy cares; joy and sorrow touch you alike. You should set grief aside, stop mourning and take food — serve the state above, and show your household strength below.

sentences.zh: 豈可縱此無益，同之兒女，傷神損識，或虧生務。

translations.literal: How can you indulge this useless grief like women and children, harming spirit and diminishing wisdom, perhaps failing in the duties of life?
translations.idiomatic: How can you indulge useless grief like a child, injuring your spirit and dulling your mind, perhaps failing in the work of life?

sentences.zh: 門下竊議，咸爲君侯不取也。」

translations.literal: We of your household privately discuss and all deem this unworthy of you, Lord."
translations.idiomatic: We of your household have discussed this privately, and all agree it ill becomes you, my lord."

sentences.zh: 余雪泣而答曰：「彭殤之達義，延吳之雅言，亦常聞之矣；

translations.literal: I, weeping through tears like snow, answered: "The enlightened meaning of 'long or short life,' Yannian and Wusheng's refined words — I have often heard them;
translations.idiomatic: I answered through tears: "The enlightened doctrine of long and short life, the fine words of Yan and Wu — I have heard them often;

sentences.zh: 顧所以未能弭意者，請陳其說。

translations.literal: yet why I cannot quiet my mind — allow me to set forth my reason.
translations.idiomatic: yet why I cannot calm my heart — let me explain.

sentences.zh: 夫植樹階庭，欽柯葉之茂；

translations.literal: When one plants a tree in the courtyard, one delights in the fullness of branch and leaf;
translations.idiomatic: Plant a tree in the courtyard and you delight in its leafy branches;

sentences.zh: 爲山累仞，惜覆簣之功。

translations.literal: building a mountain to many ren, one cherishes even the work of a basket overturned.
translations.idiomatic: raise a mountain nine ren high and you regret even one basket spilled.

sentences.zh: 故秀而不實，尼父爲之歎息；

translations.literal: Thus 'flowering yet bearing no fruit' — the Master sighed for it;
translations.idiomatic: That is why Confucius sighed over 'flowering without fruit';

sentences.zh: 析彼歧路，楊子所以留連。

translations.literal: parting at the forked road — Yangzi lingered therefore.
translations.idiomatic: and why Yangzi lingered at the parting of the roads.

sentences.zh: 事有可深，聖賢靡抑。

translations.literal: When a matter admits of deep feeling, even sages do not restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: When feeling runs deep, even sages do not forbid it.

sentences.zh: 今吾所悲，亦以悱始逾立歲，孝悌之至，自幼而長，文章之美，得之天然，好學不倦，居無塵雜，多所著述，盈帙滿笥，淡然得失之際，不見喜慍之容。

translations.literal: What I mourn is this: Fei had just passed twenty; filial piety and brotherly respect reached their height, growing from childhood; literary grace came by nature; he loved learning without weariness; his dwelling was free of worldly dust; he wrote extensively, scrolls and cases overflowing; in the face of gain and loss he was tranquil, showing neither joy nor anger.
translations.idiomatic: What I mourn is that Fei had just passed twenty: filial and respectful from childhood, gifted in letters by nature, tireless in study, living without worldly clutter, writing until scrolls and cases overflowed, calm in gain and loss, never showing joy or anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 及翰飛東朝，參伍盛列，其所遊往，皆一時才俊，賦詩頌詠，終日忘疲。

translations.literal: When he took wing in the Eastern Court, ranking among the foremost, those he consorted with were all talents of the age; composing and chanting poetry, he forgot fatigue all day long.
translations.idiomatic: When he rose in the Eastern Court and stood among the foremost, those he kept company with were the finest men of the day; composing and reciting poetry, he forgot weariness from morning to night.

sentences.zh: 每從容謂吾以遭逢時來，位隆任要，當應推賢下士，先物後身，然後可以報恩明主，克保元吉。

translations.literal: He would calmly tell me that having met with the times and risen to high rank and weighty duty, one should promote the worthy and defer to gentlemen, putting others before oneself — only then could one repay the enlightened lord and secure great fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He would calmly tell me that having risen in fortunate times to high rank and heavy responsibility, one must promote the worthy, defer to men of talent, and put others first — only then could one repay the enlightened sovereign and keep fortune secure.

sentences.zh: 俾余二紀之中，忝竊若是，幸無大過者，繄此子之助焉。

translations.literal: That in two decades I have undeservedly held such rank yet fortunately committed no great fault — it was through this son's help.
translations.idiomatic: That in twenty years I have held such rank unworthily yet avoided great fault — I owe to this son.

sentences.zh: 自出閩區，政存清靜，冀其旋反，少慰衰暮，言念今日，眇然長往。

translations.literal: Since he left for Min lands, his governance was marked by quiet purity; I hoped for his return to comfort my declining years — thinking of today, he has departed forever.
translations.idiomatic: Since he left for Min, his rule was quiet and clean; I hoped for his return to comfort my old age — but today he is gone forever.

sentences.zh: 加以闔棺千里之外，未知歸骨之期，雖復無情之倫，庸詎不痛於昔！

translations.literal: Added to this, the coffin is closed a thousand li away; the day of returning his bones is unknown — though one were utterly without feeling, how could one not grieve as in times past!
translations.idiomatic: And now the coffin is sealed a thousand li away, with no knowing when his bones will return — even the hardest heart could not but grieve as men have always grieved!

sentences.zh: 夷甫孩抱中物，尚盡慟以待賓；

translations.literal: Xiangfu, for a child still in arms, yet fully mourned to receive guests;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, for a child still in swaddling clothes, mourned fully before receiving guests;

sentences.zh: 安仁未及七旬，猶殷勤於詞賦。

translations.literal: Anren, before seventy days had passed, still poured feeling into rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: Pan An, before seventy days had passed, still poured his grief into verse.

sentences.zh: 況夫名立宦成，半途而廢者，亦焉可已已哉。

translations.literal: How much more when fame is established and office achieved, yet cut off midway — how can grief be restrained!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when name and office were established and then cut short midway — how can grief be stilled!

sentences.zh: 求其此懷，可謂苗實之義。

translations.literal: Seeking this feeling, one may call it the meaning of the budding and the fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Measured by that feeling, this may be called the grief of the bud that never bore fruit.

sentences.zh: 諸賢旣貽格言，喻以大理，卽日輟哀，命駕修職事焉。」

translations.literal: The worthies having bestowed maxims and instructed me in the great principle, that very day I ceased mourning, ordered my carriage, and returned to my official duties."
translations.idiomatic: When my friends had offered their wise counsel and explained the larger principle, I ceased mourning that very day, took up my carriage, and returned to my official duties."

sentences.zh: 勉善屬文，勤著述，雖當機務，下筆不休。

translations.literal: Mian was skilled at composing texts and diligent in writing; though occupied with crucial affairs, his brush never stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was a skilled writer and a prolific author; even while burdened with the most urgent state business, he never stopped writing.

sentences.zh: 嘗以起居注煩雜，乃加刪撰爲《流別起居注》六百卷；

translations.literal: Once, because the Daily Records were cumbersome and disorderly, he revised and compiled them into six hundred scrolls of "Classified Daily Records";
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Daily Records unwieldy, he revised and abridged them into six hundred scrolls entitled "Classified Daily Records";

sentences.zh: 《左丞彈事》五卷；

translations.literal: "Memorials of Impeachment by the Left Assistant Director," five scrolls;
translations.idiomatic: "Memorials of Impeachment by the Left Assistant Director," in five scrolls;

sentences.zh: 在選曹，撰《選品》五卷；

translations.literal: while in the Selection Bureau, he compiled "Ranks of Selection," five scrolls;
translations.idiomatic: while at the Selection Bureau, he compiled "Ranks of Selection" in five scrolls;

sentences.zh: 齊時，撰《太廟祝文》二卷；

translations.literal: during Qi, he compiled "Prayer Texts for the Imperial Ancestral Temple," two scrolls;
translations.idiomatic: under Qi he compiled "Prayer Texts for the Imperial Ancestral Temple" in two scrolls;

sentences.zh: 以孔釋二教殊途同歸，撰《會林》五十卷。

translations.literal: Because the Confucian and Buddhist teachings, though paths differ, return to the same end, he compiled "Forest of Convergences," fifty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Believing that Confucian and Buddhist teaching, though their paths differ, reach the same end, he compiled "Forest of Convergences" in fifty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 凡所著前後二集四十五卷，又爲《婦人集》十卷，皆行於世。

translations.literal: In all, his earlier and later collected works totaled forty-five scrolls; he also compiled "Anthology of Women," ten scrolls — all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in two series totaled forty-five scrolls, and he also compiled "Anthology of Women" in ten scrolls; all were in circulation.

sentences.zh: 大同三年，故佐史尚書左丞劉覽等詣闕陳勉行狀，請刊石紀德，卽降詔許立碑於墓云。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, the former staff officer and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Liu Lan and others came to the palace to present Mian's conduct report and requested that stone be carved to record his virtue; an edict was immediately issued permitting a stele to be erected at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, Liu Lan, former staff officer and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, and others presented a report on Mian's conduct at court and asked that a stone be carved to commemorate his virtue. An edict was promptly issued authorizing a stele at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 悱字敬業，幼聰敏，能屬文。

translations.literal: Fei, styled Jingye, in youth was clever and keen and could compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fei, whose courtesy name was Jingye, was clever as a boy and could already compose literary pieces.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎，轉太子舍人，掌書記之任。

translations.literal: He began his career as Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library and was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, holding charge of documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library and was later made Attendant of the Heir Apparent, in charge of records and correspondence.

sentences.zh: 累遷洗馬、中舍人，猶管書記。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Groom and Central Attendant, still managing documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Groom of the Heir Apparent and Central Attendant, while continuing to manage records and correspondence.

sentences.zh: 出入宮坊者歷稔，以足疾出爲湘東王友，遷晉安內史。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the palace quarters for many years, because of foot ailment he went out to serve as Companion to the King of Xiangdong and was transferred to Administrator of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He had served in the Eastern Palace for many years. Because of a foot ailment he left court to become Companion to the King of Xiangdong and was later appointed Administrator of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：徐勉少而厲志忘食，發憤脩身，慎言行，擇交遊；

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: "Xu Mian in youth steeled his will and forgot food, roused his spirit to cultivate himself, was cautious in word and deed, and chose his companions carefully;"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel of Chen, said: "In youth Xu Mian disciplined his will until he forgot to eat, roused himself to cultivate his character, was careful in speech and conduct, and chose his companions with care;"

sentences.zh: 加運屬興王，依光日月，故能明經術以綰青紫，出閭閻而取卿相。

translations.literal: added to this, fortune belonged to the rising king and he rested in the light of sun and moon; thus he could clarify classical learning to bind on purple and blue, and leave the lanes and alleys to take the rank of minister and chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: when fortune favored the founding emperor and he basked in imperial favor, he was able to master the classics and win high office, rising from common streets to minister and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及居重任，竭誠事主，動師古始，依則先王，提衡端軌，物無異議，爲梁宗臣，盛矣。

translations.literal: When he held heavy responsibility, he devoted his heart in serving his lord, taking antiquity as his teacher in every move and following the former kings as his rule; holding the balance and setting the standard straight, nothing met with dissent — as a pillar minister of Liang, how splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Once he held great office, he served his sovereign with complete devotion, taking antiquity as his guide and the former kings as his model. He held the scales of justice even, and none disputed his judgments — a pillar minister of Liang indeed, and a splendid one.
